question.knowledge_point: Identifying Points That Satisfy the Mean Value Theorem
question.problem:
Find the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for 
 $f(x)={x}^{2}-2x+5$ on the interval $[1,4].$
question.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is continuous on $[1,4]$ and differentiable on $(1,4),$ hence we can apply the mean value theorem. 

So, the mean value theorem states that there exists a $c\in (1,4)$ such that

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}.
$$

Plugging in $a=1$ and $b=4$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(c) & =\frac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1} \\  & =\frac{({4}^{2}-2\cdot 4+5)-({1}^{2}-2\cdot 1+5)}{3} \\  & =\frac{13-4}{3} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-2x+5)=2x-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{f}^{′}(c)=2c-2.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2c-2 & =3 \\ 2c & =5 \\ c & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
